claims.assertion: This was a metered RydeTAXI trip charged $40.74, of which $7.46 is an excess-distance charge for 5.29 km beyond the quoted route (F5, F8): on a meter service extra kilometres flow straight into the fare, so route deviation is a fare issue here.

The GPS track shows two off-route segments: 18:17–18:23 added 2.98 km (up to 1705 m off the optimal route) and 18:26–18:31 added 1.70 km (up to 1416 m off); total actual 19.5 km vs optimal 14.2 km (+5.3 km, +37%) (F1, F3, F4).

The rider's only pre-segment agreement was at 18:13, answering the driver's 18:12 proposal to 'go round via Lower Delta Road' with 'Sure, no problem.' (F9, F10); the chat contains only these two messages and both are timestamped (F11).

That agreement was a named-road authorisation limited to Lower Delta Road (F9) and cannot cover the second deviation at 18:26–18:31 (F4), which began 13 minutes after the driver's message and 4 minutes after the first off-route stretch ended; nothing in the chat names any road for that later stretch.

No rider message before the second segment agrees to it: the driver's own statement concedes 'The second turn-off was my GPS rerouting' (F12) — a unilateral route change decided by the driver, not the passenger, and the record places that segment 1416 m off the optimal route (F4).

The driver's claimed justification does not qualify: traffic records show no incidents near the route during the trip window (F15), and the only congestion shown is on the optimal corridor itself — CTE band 4, 30–39 km/h, and AYE band 5, 40–49 km/h (F13, F14) — which is not a band 1–2 severe-congestion record and in any case does not document the substituted stretch.

The unmetered portion of the deviation is the 1.70 km of the 18:26–18:31 segment, and at this trip's per-km rate ($27.52 ÷ 19.52 km = $1.4098/km, rounded to cents) (F8, F5) that equals $2.40, so the refund sought is the metre that segment consumed.
The waiting charge of $0.11 for 0.4 minutes is a meter waiting unit on a RydeTAXI trip and is not disputed (F6); the rider's complaint is limited to the second deviation only.

This is not an aggravated driver profile case — the driver has 818 trips in 90 days and 0 upheld route disputes (F18) — so the rider asks only for the fare attributable to the uncorrected segment, not an account flag.
